events.title: Proclamation of the People's Republic of China
events.description: Mao Zedong stood atop Tiananmen Gate in Beijing and proclaimed the founding of the People's Republic of China after the Chinese Communist Party's victory over the Nationalists in the Chinese Civil War.
events.significance: Established the government of the world's most populous nation, reshaped Cold War geopolitics, and is still celebrated annually as China's National Day.

events.title: Ford Model T Introduced
events.description: The Ford Motor Company released the first production Model T in Detroit, Michigan. Designed to be affordable and durable, it was later built on a moving assembly line.
events.significance: Made automobile ownership accessible to the middle class and transformed manufacturing, transportation, and the American landscape.

events.title: Nigeria Gains Independence
events.description: Nigeria became an independent nation within the Commonwealth, ending decades of British colonial rule, with Abubakar Tafawa Balewa serving as prime minister.
events.significance: Marked a milestone in African decolonization; Nigeria became the continent's most populous country and a major regional power.

events.title: Roger Maris Hits 61st Home Run
events.description: New York Yankees outfielder Roger Maris hit his 61st home run of the season on the final day of the regular season, surpassing Babe Ruth's 1927 single-season record of 60.
events.significance: Set one of baseball's most celebrated records, which stood until 1998, and sparked debate over record-keeping and the pressure on athletes.

events.title: Walt Disney World Opens
events.description: Walt Disney World Resort opened near Orlando, Florida, beginning with the Magic Kingdom park, which Walt Disney had planned before his death in 1966.
events.significance: Grew into the world's most visited vacation resort, transforming Florida's economy and setting a model for destination theme parks.
